newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU welcomes progress in Tajik peace talks.
newsitem.headline: EU welcomes progress in Tajik peace talks.

text.p: The European Union on Wednesday hailed the progress made in recent talks between the Tajikistan government and Islamic opposition and urged continued efforts to find a lasting peace in the central Asian region.
"The European Union welcomes the results of the latest talks in Mashad and Moscow between the Tajik government and the united Tajik opposition," the Dutch EU presidency said in a statement.
The two sides signed a military agreement in Moscow last Saturday, marking a major step towards a peace settlement.
The accord set out a four-step plan to integrate the armed opposition into the army by July 1998.

The month-long talks that preceded the deal were part of a U.N.-sponsored peace accord signed last December after four years of civil war in the former Soviet republic in which thousands of people have been killed.
"The success of the Tajik peace process is vital for the stabilisation of the entire central Asian region and the security and prosperity of its peoples," the EU said.
The EU called on all parties to cooperate with a commission for national reconciliation which had been set up to work towards a lasting peace in the area.

"The EU further calls upon all parties to the conflict to ensure the safety of United Nations and other personnel engaged in the provision of aid and assistance in Tajikistan and to avoid any hostage-taking."
A ceasefire has largely held in Tajikistan since the December accord, but Western observers say the two sides' inability to control rogue bands roaming the mountains may jeopardise peace efforts.

Diplomats say a power-sharing deal, in which seats on a new commission for national reconciliation were shared out between the government and opposition, could be explosive because it leaves no places for any other faction.
